newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican Cetes attractive in short-term - Santander.
newsitem.headline: Mexican Cetes attractive in short-term - Santander.

text.p: Santander Investment said in a report released on Friday that Mexican Cetes remain attractive despite a sharp drop in the treasury bills' yields.
"Over the short-term, Cetes remain attractive because of the peso's likely stability and positive carry relative to U.S. money markets," Santander analyst Lucia Domville wrote.
"The U.S. dollar has been in a strong upward channel this year, but the dollar-bloc currencies (including the peso) with significant positive carry have benefited even more," she wrote.
At the last Cetes auction the interest rate on the one-month paper fell 23 basis points to 19.46 percent. As recently as December 17 the one-month paper was yielding 27.37 percent.
Santander said Banco de Mexico has been using a temporary reduction in interest rates to unattractive levels to discourage long peso positions.
"Interest rates have a dual strategy -- to prevent excessive inflows of foreign capital and, conversely, to keep the currency competitive," Domville wrote.
Santander said it views investment in Cetes as a short-term currency and interest rate play, rather than a medium-term high-yield investment.
